issue.title: Chop subprocesses pay ~0.4s per tick importing gate_shell.models/agent/xprompt for two symbols in gate_shell.state
issue.description:
Discovered while planning the wait_checks chop realpath-churn fix (tale plan
"Remove O(waiters × artifacts) realpath churn from wait-dependency resolution").

Every AXE chop runs as a fresh subprocess, so its import cost is paid on every tick.
For `sase_chop_wait_checks`, `python -X importtime -c "import
sase.scripts.sase_chop_wait_checks"` (athena, 2026-09-08, loadavg ~44/64) measures
~544ms of cumulative import self-time, of which ~415ms comes from
`sase.core.wait_dependency_resolution` — almost entirely via one tiny import:

  `wait_dependency_resolution/_artifact_state.py` does
  `from sase.gate_shell.state import TERMINAL_GATE_STATES, is_real_gate_member`
  (two small symbols in a 90-line module), but importing any `sase.gate_shell.*`
  submodule executes `sase/gate_shell/__init__.py`, which eagerly imports
  `sase.gate_shell.models` (~395ms cumulative) and drags in `sase.agent` →
  `sase.agent.multi_prompt` → `sase.xprompt` (~258ms) plus jsonschema and jinja2.
  `sase.gate_shell.state` itself also imports `sase.agent.status_buckets`, which
  triggers the `sase.agent` package `__init__`.

The wait_checks chop is fs-triggered with a 120s quiet backstop, so under agent load
this ~0.4-0.5s tax recurs continuously, and it inflates further on loaded/low-resource
hosts (import time scales with CPU contention). Other chop subprocesses and short-lived
CLI entry points that touch these packages pay the same tax.

Remediation direction (root cause is measured; strategy has design leeway, hence
large): apply the sase-ou pattern — closed task sase-ou made `sase/core/__init__.py`
lazy via `sase._lazy_exports` (lazy_getattr/lazy_dir) — to `sase/gate_shell/__init__.py`
(and evaluate `sase/agent/__init__.py`), or otherwise decouple light leaf modules like
`sase.gate_shell.state` / `sase.agent.status_buckets` from their packages' heavy eager
`__init__` imports. Re-measure with `-X importtime` after; the wait_checks chop importer
should drop from ~544ms to roughly the ~130ms non-gate_shell remainder.

task_type_fields.impact: Every fs-triggered wait_checks tick (120s max quiet) and every other chop subprocess importing these packages pays ~0.4-0.5s of startup, worse under load — exactly the low-resource/high-load hosts where prompt wait resolution matters most
